stem: A prompt asks a chat model for the total cost of a shipment after weight tiers, a fuel surcharge and a discount. Asked for the number directly, the model often returns a wrong total, although each single rule is applied correctly when asked alone. Which prompt change most directly helps?

choices.text: Ask for the total in a single line of at most five words so that the answer cannot drift
Tell the model that its answer is very important and that it must not make any mistakes in the total
Ask the model to work through each rule step by step and then give the final total on a last line
Move the pricing rules to the end of the prompt, since the last instruction is always the one followed

stem: A developer sends a `json_schema` `response_format` to a Foundation Model APIs chat endpoint. In the schema the `currency` property has a regex `pattern` and `price` uses `anyOf` to accept either a string or a number. The request is rejected or the constraints are not applied, and the team still needs schema-conforming JSON. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Use plain `string` and `number` properties, list the allowed currency codes in the field description, and validate in code
Keep the schema and switch `type` to `json_object`, which applies the schema's regular expression during decoding
Declare `price` as `"type": ["string", "number"]`, since a list of types replaces `anyOf` in this subset
Move the `anyOf` branches into a `$ref` definition, since references express alternatives

stem: A prompt asks a chat model to label support tickets as `billing`, `outage` or `other`. Replies vary between "Billing", "This looks like a billing issue" and "billing." Which TWO changes most directly make the output a single, stable label? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Raise the temperature to 2 so the model explores more phrasings and settles on one
Set the temperature to 0 so that sampling is deterministic and the same ticket gets the same reply each time
Add "be creative with the label wording" to the system message to prompt a consistent style
Increase `max_tokens` so that the model has enough room to finish its explanation before the label
Include two or three example tickets in the prompt, each followed by exactly the label text the application expects

stem: A support assistant must always answer in Korean, in at most three bullet points, and never speculate beyond the supplied context. Each turn carries a new user question and new retrieved passages. Where should these standing rules live in the chat request?

choices.text: In the first user message only, relying on later turns to remember them without repeating
In a one-time setup request per session, because the endpoint stores them for later calls
In an assistant message placed before the first user turn so the model treats them as its own earlier output
In the system message, with only the question and passages sent in each user message

stem: A tool lets analysts paste any text and name whichever fields they want extracted (for example "supplier, due date" one day and "diagnosis, dosage" the next). The field list is not known at development time, but the reply must always be valid JSON. Which `response_format` fits?

choices.text: A `json_schema` using `anyOf` so that each analyst's field list becomes its own branch
`{"type": "json_object"}` with the requested field names given in the prompt
Plain text, then a regular expression in application code that pulls the key-value pairs
A `json_schema` that lists every field name any analyst might ask for, all marked optional

stem: A team uses a `json_schema` response format with five fields and `max_tokens=64`. Short documents give correct objects, but for long documents the JSON stops in the middle of a string and fails to parse. What is the fix?

choices.text: Raise `max_tokens` above the length of the largest expected object
Raise the temperature so the model produces a more compact object for long documents
Add a stop sequence at the closing brace so the model ends the object itself
Remove `response_format` so the model is free to shorten its output

stem: A helpdesk wants to show agents the five past tickets that are closest in meaning to a new ticket, even when no keywords match. Which model task should the application use?

choices.text: A chat model that is asked to recall similar tickets from its training data and list their numbers
A classification model that assigns every ticket one of a fixed set of categories and matches on the category
An embedding model that turns tickets and the new ticket into vectors, ranked by similarity
A summarization function that shortens each ticket, followed by a keyword match on the summaries

stem: Analysts must assign each of three million rows in a Unity Catalog table to one of six topic labels using SQL. They have no prompt-engineering experience and want the least setup. Which option fits best?

choices.text: `ai_extract` with a schema that has six boolean fields, one per label
`ai_query` with a hand-written prompt and a custom parser for each model reply
A custom classifier that the team trains and deploys on a model serving endpoint
The task-specific `ai_classify` function with the six labels as an argument

stem: Which TWO requirements are best served by an embedding model rather than by a chat model? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Translate product descriptions into Portuguese
Draft a polite written reply to a customer complaint in the brand's established tone of voice
Group thousands of news articles by topic using distances between vectors
Summarize a one-hour call transcript into five bullet points
Find knowledge-base articles that are semantically close to a user's question

stem: A back-office team stores scanned supplier invoices as PDFs in a Unity Catalog volume. Before any language-model step they need the text, tables and layout of each page as structured content they can query with SQL. Which function is built for this?

choices.text: `ai_parse_document`, which parses text, tables and layout from unstructured documents
An embedding model, which converts every page into a vector the team can query with SQL
`ai_summarize`, applied directly to each PDF file path
`ai_translate`, which renders the invoice content as plain text in the target language

stem: Employees ask questions about internal HR policies that change every week. Answers must reflect the latest version and name the policy they came from. Which design meets this need?

choices.text: Use only an embedding model, returning the vector of the closest policy as the answer
Fine-tune a chat model on the policy documents each month and let the model answer from what it learned
Classify every question into one policy ID and return the stored policy text without a language model
Retrieve the matching policy passages for each question and pass them to a chat model as context

stem: A team builds a RAG chain whose input is the user's question as a string and whose output is the answer as a string. Which component order produces this?

choices.text: Prompt template, embedding model for the whole prompt, then chat model that returns the passages
Retriever, then a prompt template merging passages and question, then the chat model, then a parser
Retriever, then an output parser on the raw passages, then the chat model without a prompt template
Chat model first, then the retriever on its answer, then a prompt template that formats the text

stem: A LangChain chain ends with a chat model. The result is a message object, but the downstream SQL writer expects a plain Python string in a column. Which component should be added after the model?

choices.text: A string output parser (`StrOutputParser`)
A prompt template with a `{content}` variable
A second embedding model to flatten the message
A retriever over the answers table

stem: A team's chain fails with an error about missing input variables. ``` prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template( "Context: {context}\nQuestion: {question}") chain = prompt | llm | StrOutputParser() chain.invoke({"input": "What is the refund window?"}) ``` What is the correct fix?

choices.text: Increase the model's context window so that the template's variables fit in the request
Replace the chat model with a larger one that fills in missing variables itself
Wrap the retriever in an output parser and rename both template variables to `input`
Add a first dict step: `context` from the retriever, `question` from the input

stem: A RAG chain must return its answer together with the source of each passage it used. Which TWO changes support this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Raise the temperature so the model recalls where the information likely came from
Add a string output parser, which looks up the sources of the answer on its own
Return the title and URL columns from the retrieval step along with each chunk's text
Replace the chat model with an embedding model that also reports the sources
Format every passage with its title and URL in the prompt and tell the model to cite them

stem: In a multi-turn RAG chatbot, the first question "What is the parental leave policy?" is answered well. The follow-up "And for contractors?" returns unrelated passages. Which chain component should be added?

choices.text: A larger top-k setting on the retriever, so many more passages come back for the follow-up
A step where the chat model rewrites the follow-up, with history, into a standalone question
A lower temperature on the answer model, so it ignores the unrelated passages
A larger embedding dimension, so the short follow-up has more room to hold context

stem: Sales reps lose hours searching past RFP answers. The team wants a GenAI assistant that cuts that time. Which input/output description is the best translation of this goal for the pipeline?

choices.text: Input: the name of the model to use; output: a benchmark accuracy score for the model
Input: a monthly table of all RFPs; output: a summary report mailed to sales leadership
Input: the rep's question; output: an answer citing RFP documents, or "not found" if nothing is relevant
Input: all RFP documents embedded in bulk and loaded; output: a vector index with no user-facing result returned

stem: A retailer wants a sentiment label for each of 2 million reviews, refreshed nightly, written to a column of a Unity Catalog table. Nobody waits for individual answers. Which pipeline shape fits?

choices.text: A real-time endpoint called once per review by a web frontend whenever a customer opens the page
A scheduled batch job that applies an AI Function such as `ai_query` to the review column
An embedding index of the reviews, queried by a rep who types a question for each result
A chat application that streams one reply per review to a person who copies it into the table

stem: A chat interface calls a model whose full answers take about eight seconds. Users complain that the screen stays empty until the end. The business requirement is that text starts to appear within about a second. What belongs in the output specification?

choices.text: A streamed response, where the interface displays tokens as the endpoint produces them
A single JSON object returned after the model finishes, validated against a schema
A table of answers that is refreshed by a nightly job and read by the interface
A vector for each answer that the interface renders after similarity search

stem: A finance team wants invoice data in a table: supplier, invoice date and total for each PDF. Which output definition for the pipeline best serves the downstream reporting?

choices.text: A free-text paragraph describing each invoice in the model's own words, parsed later with regular expressions
A similarity score between each invoice and a reference invoice
A yes/no flag per invoice that says whether extraction succeeded
A typed record per invoice: `supplier` string, `invoice_date` ISO string, `total` number, null if absent

stem: A multinational's support assistant must answer from knowledge-base articles, but agents may only see articles for their own region. Which description of the pipeline input and behavior meets the requirement?

choices.text: Input: the question; a separate fine-tuned chat model is deployed for every region
Input: the question; output: answers for all regions, with the interface hiding the other ones
Input: question plus the agent's region; retrieval filters on the article region column
Input: the question only; the system prompt asks the model to ignore articles of other regions

stem: An agent must answer "Can customer C-88 return order 5531 under the policy?" It has three tools: `get_order` (order date and product category from a governed table), `search_policy` (retrieval over policy documents) and `check_window` (compares a date to a return window). Which sequencing is correct?

choices.text: `search_policy` with the raw question, then answer directly without calling any order or window tool
Answer from model memory, then call `get_order` to check that the order exists
`check_window` first with today's date, then `get_order`, then `search_policy` to confirm the result
`get_order`, then `search_policy` for that category, then `check_window` with the date and window

stem: A developer passes a `tools` list to a Foundation Model APIs chat endpoint. The reply contains a tool call with JSON arguments for `get_weather`, but the weather lookup never happens and the user sees no answer. What explains this?

choices.text: The caller lacks `EXECUTE` privilege on the endpoint, so the tool call is dropped
The model only proposes the call; the application must run the function and send back the result
Tools must be registered in Unity Catalog first
Pay-per-token endpoints run functions on the server side only when streaming is switched on for the request

stem: In a fixed workflow, the first model step must always call `lookup_order` before anything else, whatever the user typed. Which `tool_choice` value does this?

choices.text: `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_order"}}`
`"auto"`, the default, in which the model decides whether to call a function
`"required"`, which makes the model call at least one function of its own choice
`"none"`, which lets the model generate a user-facing message only

stem: A team exposes a SQL-backed Unity Catalog function as an agent tool. Which TWO are needed so that the agent can use it? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Serverless compute enabled in the workspace, because the Function Client runs the tool on serverless general compute
Register the function as an MLflow model version so the framework can load it
`SELECT` on every table, so the function can answer any question
Deploy the function to its own model serving endpoint before the agent can call it
The agent's identity has `EXECUTE` on the function, plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` on parents

stem: An agent must answer "How many units of SKU 91 were returned last week?" from a governed Unity Catalog table. Which tool definition is the best fit for that sub-task?

choices.text: A web-search MCP server, which returns pages that may mention returns of that SKU
An AI Search index built over text copies of the table rows, queried for the closest chunk
A Unity Catalog function that runs a parameterized SQL aggregate over the table
No tool: the chat model estimates the figure from patterns in its training data

stem: A team has an agent written with its own Python framework. Long research runs sometimes die when the host restarts, and the team wants managed hosting without rewriting the agent. Which Agent Bricks capability fits?

choices.text: Databricks Sandbox, which gives code written by the agent an isolated place to run
Agent Runtime with AgentKit, which hosts any framework and adds durable execution that survives restarts
MLflow Tracing, which records every step of a run and automatically replays the failed step after the host comes back
A Genie Agent, which would replace the custom framework with a data environment configured by the data team

stem: Finance analysts want a business-user assistant that answers natural-language questions about governed sales tables. The data team wants to configure trusted data, metrics and business rules and does not want to write agent code. Which option fits best?

choices.text: An AI Search index over the text columns of the tables, queried by a prompt template that contains the question
An `ai_query` call run once per table row, which would write each answer into a new table
An agent scaffolded with the Agent Bricks CLI, with SQL generation written by the team in Python
A Genie Agent configured by the data team with the sales tables, metrics and business rules

stem: Forty thousand supplier contracts sit as PDFs in a Unity Catalog volume. A scheduled SQL job must write vendor, contract term and renewal date for each contract to a table. No interactive chat is needed. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Stand up a conversational agent on Agent Runtime and ask it about each contract, one at a time, at run time
Have an agent write OCR scripts that run in Databricks Sandbox once for every file in the volume
Index the PDFs in an AI Search index and run a hybrid query for each field of each contract
Parse the files with `ai_parse_document`, then pass the output to `ai_extract` with a three-field schema

stem: Which TWO statements about Agent Bricks as the docs describe it today are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Knowledge Assistant is the recommended starting point for every new low-code agent over documents and data
Agent Runtime can host agents built with any framework, whether the agent is stateful or stateless
Code that an agent writes runs best inside the agent's own process, so Sandbox is meant only for human-written code
Agents must be built with the Knowledge Assistant builder before Agent Runtime can host them
MLflow Tracing records each step an agent takes, and traces can be stored and governed at scale in Unity Catalog

stem: A team must build a new system in which one orchestrating agent routes questions to a Genie Agent, a Unity Catalog function and an MCP server. The routing needs custom Python logic and unit tests in CI. Which route do the docs recommend for a new system?

choices.text: Write the orchestrator in code with the Agent Bricks CLI, call the subagents as tools, and deploy it on Agent Runtime
Chain `ai_query` calls in a SQL script so that every question goes through each subagent in sequence
Build it on the Supervisor Agent offering, which the docs recommend for new systems
Create one Knowledge Assistant per subagent and chain them by pasting each answer into the next prompt by hand

stem: A contract-search RAG index was built by cutting every document into 800-character pieces with a fixed-size splitter. Retrieved chunks often start in the middle of a sentence and end in the middle of the next clause, and answers cite half a clause. What is the best change to the chunking step?

choices.text: Lower the embedding dimension so that each cut piece carries less ambiguity about its meaning in the index
Raise the chunk size to the whole document so that no clause is ever cut
Switch to a recursive splitter that prefers paragraph and sentence boundaries before it cuts by length
Keep the 800-character pieces but remove every period so that sentences cannot be split

stem: A user question needs an exception that is stated in the first sentence of the next chunk. Retrieval returns the earlier chunk, so the answer omits the exception. The team keeps the chunk size but wants to lower the chance that facts at a boundary are separated. Which change fits?

choices.text: Raise the embedding dimension so that the two chunks become more similar to each other
Cut each chunk to a single sentence so that any exception becomes its own chunk
Remove the overlap and rely on a deduplication job to repair the cuts afterwards
Add a modest overlap between adjacent chunks so that text near each boundary appears in both

stem: Product specification PDFs contain tables of limits and tolerances, and users ask about values in those tables. The current character splitter cuts tables in the middle of rows and returns fragments with no column names. Which approach to chunking fits the document structure?

choices.text: Flatten every table into one long line of cell values and chunk it with the same splitter as the prose
Treat each table element apart from prose, split only between rows, and repeat the header in every piece
Set the chunk size to 8,000 characters for the whole corpus so that most tables fit inside one chunk
Drop the tables from the corpus because numbers and column grids do not embed well

stem: A RAG assistant must show, next to each answer, the file name and section title of the passages it used. The chunk table currently has only a chunk id and the chunk text. How should the chunking step be changed?

choices.text: Rely on the embedding vectors, which can be decoded back into the file name
Ask the chat model to guess the source from the wording of each chunk when it writes the answer
Write source path, section title and page as extra columns next to each chunk's text and index them
Add the file name to the prompt template by hand, so that the model always names the same file

stem: Parsed PDF manuals still include the running page header ("Acme Router Guide - Confidential"), the footer and the page number on every page. Retrieval for many different questions returns chunks dominated by that repeated text. What should the engineer do before chunking?

choices.text: Drop the page header, page footer and page number elements from the parsed output before chunking
Remove common words from the parsed text so that the header phrase loses its weight
Convert all text to lowercase so that the repeated header is not matched as strongly
Increase the number of results returned so that useful chunks outrank the repeated headers

stem: A knowledge base was copied into several shared drives. For many questions the top five chunks are the same paragraph repeated from different copies, so the model receives one fact five times and misses the others. Which preprocessing step addresses the cause?

choices.text: Switch to a larger embedding model so that identical text receives more varied vectors across the different copies
Raise the temperature of the chat model so that the repeated retrieved text produces more varied answers
Reduce the chunk size so that fewer words repeat inside each one of the retrieved chunks in the top results
Deduplicate documents before chunking, with metadata for exact copies and MinHash joins for near duplicates

stem: A policy library holds every revision of each policy: drafts, approved versions and superseded versions. Users complain that answers quote rules that were replaced last year. The ingested table has `status` and `effective_date` columns. Which filter step fits the pipeline?

choices.text: Keep only approved documents with the latest effective date for each policy before chunking
Compress each revision into a summary and embed all summaries together in a single index
Keep only the first revision of each policy because it is the most stable version over time
Keep every revision and ask the chat model to prefer the most recent one in the system prompt

stem: Scanned manuals were parsed with `ai_parse_document`. Some elements contain garbled text from smudged pages, and the model sometimes quotes it. Each parsed element has a `confidence` value from 0 to 1. What is the best way to keep the garbage out of the index?

choices.text: Embed all elements anyway, because the embedding model can recover the meaning of garbled text
Keep only the first element of every page, since the first element is the most reliable
Filter or review elements whose `confidence` is below a threshold chosen from a sample of the parsed output
Delete every `figure` element, since figures are the only elements that can hold unreliable text

stem: A team runs a notebook on a cluster and wants an open-source Python library that partitions mixed Word and PDF files into typed elements such as titles, narrative text and tables. They do not want to use AI Functions. Which library fits?

choices.text: `matplotlib`, which reads Word and PDF files into charts and sections
`unstructured`, an off-the-shelf library for parsing documents of various formats
`BeautifulSoup`, which parses Word and PDF files by walking their tag trees
`scikit-learn`, whose vectorizers split Word and PDF files into titles and tables

stem: Thousands of photographs of printed warning labels are stored as JPG files. A notebook must turn them into text before chunking. Which tool category fits?

choices.text: `PyPDF2`, which reads text from any file containing a picture of printed text
`BeautifulSoup`, which reads the text printed on each image through its tag selectors
A tokenizer from a language model library, which converts each image into word tokens directly
An OCR engine such as Tesseract (or a managed OCR service), which reads text from images

stem: A corpus has help-center pages saved as HTML and manuals saved as PDF files that have a selectable text layer. Which TWO libraries fit the extraction step? (Select TWO)

choices.text: `scikit-learn` `TfidfVectorizer` to read the page text out of the HTML files
`NLTK` `word_tokenize` to pull the text out of the PDF files
`PyPDF2` (or `unstructured`) to read text from the PDF files
`Tesseract` OCR to read the HTML pages, which are always rendered as images
`BeautifulSoup` (or `lxml`) to select the body elements of the HTML pages

stem: A volume holds PDF, DOCX and PPTX files, many with tables and charts. The team wants layout-aware output (tables as HTML, headers, footers, figure descriptions) at scale, from SQL, with the data staying inside the Databricks security perimeter. Which extraction option fits?

choices.text: An OCR engine hosted by an external SaaS provider and called once for each page
The `ai_parse_document` AI Function on a binary column read from the volume in SQL
A Python script that loops over files with `PyPDF2` on the driver
`BeautifulSoup`, applied to the XML inside the DOCX and PPTX files

stem: A batch job turns PDFs in a Unity Catalog volume into an AI Search index for RAG. Which order of operations is correct?

choices.text: Read the files, parse them, chunk the text, add a chunk id, write a Delta table with change data feed, then create the index
Parse the files, create the index, add a unique id per chunk, then chunk the text and write the Delta table
Create the Delta Sync index, read the files, write the raw files into it, and let the index chunk them
Chunk the raw bytes, parse each chunk, create the index, then write the chunks to a Delta table

stem: A job writes chunks to a new managed Delta table with `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT`. Creating a Delta Sync index on a standard AI Search endpoint over that table fails with an error about the source table's change tracking. What is the fix?

choices.text: Enable change data feed on the table (`delta.enableChangeDataFeed = true`), then create the index
Switch the embedding model to a larger one that supports more input columns
Convert the table to a view so that the endpoint reads the chunks directly from the storage
Rename the chunk text column so that it does not clash with the vector column

stem: Every night the pipeline overwrites the whole chunk table with chunks for all 2 million documents, although only a few hundred documents changed. The Delta Sync index then re-processes everything and the run is slow. Which change to the write step fits?

choices.text: Write the chunks to a CSV file in the volume so that overwriting does not touch the table
Split the chunk table into a separate table for every document so that overwrites are smaller
Re-chunk only changed documents and apply their chunks with MERGE, removing the old chunks of those documents
Keep overwriting, but move the table to a different catalog so that the index sees fewer changed rows

stem: Which TWO design choices are correct for a chunk table that will back an AI Search Delta Sync Index? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Name the primary key column `_id`, since AI Search expects this name for the key
Give every chunk row its own unique primary key, so that a changed chunk can be updated in the index
Store the text only in the index, with a source table that holds vectors but no text column at all
Use the source file name as the primary key, since all chunks of a file share one name
Keep the chunk text and its metadata columns in the same table so that filters can use the metadata

stem: Before building an HR assistant, a team has a drive with 30,000 files and wants to know whether the corpus can actually answer what employees ask. Which first step fits?

choices.text: Embed all files and look at the sizes of the resulting vectors to decide whether coverage is enough
Count the file types in the drive and keep the type that has the most files, since volume means coverage
Ask the chat model to say whether the corpus is complete, based on a list of file names
Collect employee questions with domain experts and check that each one can be answered from some document

stem: An audit asks which original file produced a passage that a RAG assistant quoted. The pipeline currently reads documents straight from a SharePoint site on every run, parses them in memory and writes only chunks. The original files change often. How should ingestion change?

choices.text: Land the raw files in Unity Catalog first, keep them with source path and timestamps, and parse from there
Delete the SharePoint originals after chunking so that only one version of every document remains
Store only the embedding vectors, since each vector identifies the document that it was computed from
Keep parsing in memory, but write the chunk text into the application log so that it can be searched later

stem: Two sources describe the refund policy. One is a wiki page last edited four years ago by an unknown author. The other is a PDF from the legal team with a version number and an effective date. Answers must be correct and defensible. Which approach follows good corpus practice?

choices.text: Index only the wiki page, because wiki pages are easier to parse than PDF files
Index both sources equally and let retrieval pick the best match for each question
Index the wiki page only, because it is longer and so contains more detail on the refund rules
Index the legal PDF as the authoritative source and keep its version and effective date as metadata

stem: A team is choosing documents for a customer-support assistant. Which TWO checks show that a candidate document set belongs in the corpus? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The documents contain the product name in the title, so the text is guaranteed to be on topic
The documents answer questions that real customers ask, as confirmed by support staff or sampled tickets
The documents are already stored as PDF files, because PDF is the best-supported format
The set is the largest collection available, since more text always improves the answers
The content is current and reliable, with an owner who can confirm it is still valid

stem: A retriever returns five chunks for an evaluation question. Two of them are relevant. The labeled evaluation set says four chunks in the whole index are relevant to this question. What are precision@5 and recall@5 for this question?

choices.text: Precision@5 is 0.5 and recall@5 is 0.4
Precision@5 is 0.8 and recall@5 is 0.4
Precision@5 is 0.4 and recall@5 is 0.5
Precision@5 is 0.4 and recall@5 is 0.8

stem: Two retrievers both find the one relevant chunk within the top ten results for 90% of questions. Retriever X usually places it first and retriever Y usually places it ninth, and the LLM sees only the first three chunks. Which metric reveals the difference?

choices.text: Recall@10, which counts a relevant chunk equally at any position within the top ten
Hit rate@10, which gives full credit whenever a relevant chunk is anywhere in the top ten
Mean reciprocal rank (MRR), which averages 1 divided by the rank of the first relevant result
Index size, which is the same for both retrievers because they use the same corpus

stem: A team wrote its own retriever function that returns rows with columns named `chunk_id`, `body` and `source_path`. In MLflow traces the retrieval step is not recognized as a retrieval, so retrieval judges do not run automatically and no source links appear. What should the team do?

choices.text: Trace it as a RETRIEVER span and map its columns with `mlflow.models.set_retriever_schema`
Disable tracing, because retrieval judges only run against untraced agents
Rename the retriever function to `retrieve`, which MLflow detects automatically by function name
Switch the chat model to a larger one, since only larger models can read custom retriever columns

stem: A team has 150 evaluation questions with the reference answer for each. They want to compute recall@k for their retriever, but the evaluation set holds no information about which documents hold the answers. What must be added to the evaluation set?

choices.text: The embedding vector of every question, computed by the production embedding model
For each question, the identifiers (such as `doc_uri`) of the documents that contain its answer
The latency measured for every question, since slow queries probably match fewer documents
A second reference answer for each question, written in a different style
